title.narrative: INTOSAI IDI Development Initiative 2025-2028 - INTOSAI-IDI 2025-2028 - Ny strategi 2024

description.narrative:
Intosai Development Initiative (IDI) is a non-profit and independent part of the International Organisation of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI), which is an umbrella organization for Supreme Audit Institutions from 195 countries. IDI's mandate is to support Supreme Audit Institutions in developing countries. As part of INTOSAI, they have an unique role as a trusted partner to Supreme Audit Institutions worldwide. IDI will continue its work under six work streams - Independent, Well-governed, Relevant and Professional SAIs, Global Foundations and Bilateral Support - and with integrating gender equality and inclusion in all IDI´s operations. Work and achievements in each of these work-streams will contribute to the Strategic Plan´s three overarching strategic priorities (Outcomes): Sustainability, Digitalisation and Public Trust in SAIs. A new impetus is an even stronger focus on predictability and long-term approach in the support to SAIs.
Each IDI work-stream contributes to the strategic plan by delivering on specific initiatives (as outlined in the application) to support SAI development, either initiatives focused on individual or a group of SAIs, or with a global approach to strengthen SAIs in developing countries and their institutional and enabling environment.

Intosai Development Initiative (IDI) är en ideell och oberoende del av Internationella organisationen för högsta revisionsorgan (INTOSAI), som är en paraplyorganisation för högsta revisionsorgan i 195 länder. IDI:s uppdrag är att stärka kapaciteten hos högsta revisionsorgan i utvecklingsländer. Som en del av INTOSAI har de en unik roll som en betrodd partner till högsta revisionsorgan världen över. IDI kommer att fortsätta sitt arbete inom sex arbetsområden – Oberoende, Välstyrda, Relevanta och Professionella högsta revisionsorgan, Globala grunder och Bilateralt stöd – samt med att integrera jämställdhet och inkludering i alla IDI:s verksamheter. Arbetet och resultaten inom vart och ett av dessa arbetsområden kommer att bidra till den strategiska planens tre övergripande strategiska prioriteringar (resultat): Hållbarhet, Digitalisering och Allmänhetens förtroende för högsta revisionsorgan. En ny drivkraft är ett ännu starkare fokus på förutsägbarhet och ett långsiktigt angreppssätt i stödet till högsta revisionsorgan. Varje arbetsområde inom IDI bidrar till den strategiska planen genom att leverera specifika initiativ (som beskrivs i ansökan) för att stödja utvecklingen av högsta revisionsorgan, antingen initiativ som är inriktade på ett enskilt eller en grupp av högsta revisionsorgan, eller med ett globalt angreppssätt för att stärka den institutionella och möjliggörande miljön för högsta revisionsorgan i utvecklingsländer i allmänhet.

The overall objective of IDI´s strategic plan is "Independent, credible and sustainable SAIs for better societies and improved lives."
For that objective to be achieved IDI has identified three strategic priorities: Sustainability, Digitalization and Public Trust in SAIs.
The strategic priorities are translated into three outcomes:
• Sustainably governed SAIs, with sustainable audit practices, contributing to sustainable development • Digitalization: SAIs enhancing the use of technology in SAI governance and in SAI audit practices, and contributing to better use of technology by governments • Public trust in SAIs: SAI institutional strengthening, enhancing SAI strategic stakeholder engagement, and demonstrating SAI value
IDI measure results on four different levels:
Impact: Indicators related to changes at the country level to which SAIs contribute, such as action on audit recommendations, compliance with laws and regulations, public trust in government, and stakeholder engagement in accountability. IDI monitors these indicators as they are within its sphere of concern but does not set targets as they are so far removed from IDIs influence.
Example of expected results on the impact level:
- % of countries in which a Committee of the Legislature examines the Audit Report on the annual budget within six months of its availability, and publish a report with findings and recommendations
- % of countries in which a formal, comprehensive, and timely response was made by the executive or the audited entity on audits for which follow-up was expected during the last three completed fiscal years
Long-Term Outcomes: Indicators where the expected result of an IDI initiative is a measured, direct improvement in the outputs of participating SAIs, against a defined benchmark. This includes SAI reporting and publication, quality and coverage of SAI audits, and engagement with external stakeholders. IDI has some influence on these indicators, though they rely heavily on factors under the control or influence of SAIs.
Example of expected results on the long-term outcome level:
- Cumulative number of cases where IDI support contributes to improved SAI outputs from sustainable audit practices
- Cumulative number of cases where IDI support contributes to improved SAI outputs on enhancing the use of technology in SAI audit practices
- Cumulative number of cases where IDI support contributes to SAI outputs that contribute to stronger SAI strategic stakeholder engagement
Short-Term Outcomes: These indicators focus on intended SAI capacity improvements to which IDI initiatives contribute. This includes SAI institutional capacity, organisational systems capacity and professional staff capacity. These lie within IDIs influence but not under its control.
Example of expected results on short-term outcome level:
- Cumulative number of cases where IDI support contributes to improved SAI capacity for sustainable audit practices
- Cumulative number of cases where IDI support contributes to improved SAI capacity to use technology in their governance practices
- Cumulative number of cases where IDI support contributes to SAIs strengthening their capacity to demonstrate their value to the public
IDI Outputs: These indicators measure results over which IDI has significant but not absolute control. It includes intermediate steps carried out by an SAI (with IDI support) which are part of efforts to enhance SAI performance, but do not on their own constitute a performance improvement. It also measures IDIs internal results, such as overall participation of SAIs, SAI teams and SAI staff in IDI initiatives, progress in becoming a more sustainable and efficient organisation, mobilisation of in-kind support, and IDIs partnerships with and support to organisations other than SAIs.
Example of results on output level:
- Number of developing country SAIs benefitting from long-term, SAI-level support delivered by IDI (during the year)
- Current number of published IDI products for the ultimate benefit of SAIs (each language of publication counted as one product)
- Whether IDI: has a permanent focal point for gender and inclusion; has a gender and inclusion team (champions) across IDI; reports annually on its gender balance; and prioritises gender-balance and inclusion in its recruitment processes (100% if all criteria met)
